summary: StarNews Mobile, an African mobile video network founded by Guy Kamgaing in 2017, raised $3 million in a pre-Series A round led by Janngo Capital, with French soccer players among the investors. The platform lets African creators monetize content through subscriptions sold via telecom partners like MTN and Orange, paid with airtime. It has over 4 million active subscribers and plans to expand to 11 markets by next year.
one_line: StarNews Mobile raised a $3M pre-Series A led by Janngo Capital, with French soccer stars joining, to grow its telco-distributed African creator video platform.
key_facts: StarNews Mobile secured $3 million in pre-Series A funding, led by Janngo Capital.
StarNews operates in six African countries: Cameroon (where it started), Nigeria, Ghana, Congo, Benin and Ivory Coast.
Guy Kamgaing, a Los Angeles-based Cameroonian and ex-PwC consultant, founded StarNews in 2017 after about 10 years in content monetization and VAS (Value-Added Services).
StarNews has over 4 million active subscribers via partnerships with MTN and Orange, and more than 120 content creators.
StarNews exited South Africa after a misalignment with MTN's strategy for engaging content creators.
Including this round, StarNews has raised nearly $8 million, including a $900,000 friends and family round, a $2 million seed and a $1.8 million extension.
Users pay with airtime for bundles, weekly subscriptions and daily plans across six different networks.
At the 2021 African Cup of Nations (AFCON), exclusive content brought 600,000 new users, and a Fally Ipupa concert offer attracted 500,000 subscribers.
StarNews's billing rate, the number of people with enough airtime to pay for digital services, is three times higher in Nigeria than in Francophone markets.
StarNews paid $1 million to creators last year, averaging about $70,000 per month, and has 40 employees.
StarNews aims to be in 11 markets by next year, expanding to Nigeria and Ghana while strengthening its presence in Francophone Africa.
Soccer players Aurélien Tchouaméni (Real Madrid), Jules Koundé (Barcelona) and Mike Maignan (AC Milan), all linked to Excellence Sport Nation, invested in the round.
Fatoumata Bâ of Janngo Capital said Africa's creative industry is poised for fourfold expansion by 2050 and up to $20 billion in GDP.
